policy: The published 20-photo lineup is fixed. Each milestone follows its photograph by record ID; pairing fidelity takes precedence over forcing the photographs into strict date order, so neighboring milestone dates may overlap.

milestones.headline: Native peoples make the San Gorgonio Pass their homeland
milestones.context: The Morongo council house opens the story with the Native communities whose cultural life in the Pass long predates the city of Beaumont.

sources.label: City of Beaumont, Existing Conditions Report
Morongo Band of Mission Indians — About Us

milestones.headline: Pauline Weaver and his partners petition for Rancho San Gorgonio
milestones.context: Weaver, Isaac Williams and Wallace Woodruff petitioned for the former mission rancho, took possession without a completed grant, and ran cattle in the Pass.

sources.label: City of Banning General Plan — Cultural Resources
Library of Congress — Michael C. White narrative

milestones.headline: The railroad town of San Gorgonio becomes Beaumont
milestones.context: The townsite was established beside the railroad in 1884, renamed Beaumont in 1886, and officially surveyed and filed in 1887; the 1907 street view shows the commercial town that followed.

sources.label: City of Beaumont General Plan — historic setting
Calisphere — Egan Avenue, 1907

milestones.headline: A larger Southern Pacific depot anchors the growing town
milestones.context: The depot linked Beaumont to regional markets and travel while concentrating hotels, stores, warehouses and civic life near the tracks.

sources.label: Calisphere — Southern Pacific depot, Beaumont

milestones.headline: Beaumont’s rail yard keeps Southern Pacific traffic moving
milestones.context: Shop crews, locomotives, fuel tanks and yard facilities made Beaumont a working railroad service point, not merely a passenger stop.

sources.label: Calisphere — Southern Pacific engines at Beaumont

milestones.headline: Fifth and Egan become Beaumont’s commercial crossroads
milestones.context: The post office, San Gorgonio Mercantile Company and pool hall clustered at the intersection that became the young town’s business center.

sources.label: Calisphere — Fifth Street and Egan Avenue
Beaumont Library District — Local History

milestones.headline: Grain ranching drives Beaumont’s first agricultural economy
milestones.context: Reznor Perry Stewart’s large grain-and-hay operation represents the dry-farming economy that preceded Beaumont’s orchard boom.

sources.label: City of Beaumont, Existing Conditions Report
Calisphere — Stewart Ranch grain harvest

milestones.headline: The Morongo Reservation is established in the Pass
milestones.context: A presidential executive order created the reservation; the traditional kish records the continuity of Cahuilla daily life there around 1900.

sources.label: Morongo Band of Mission Indians — About Us
Calisphere — traditional house on Morongo Reservation

milestones.headline: Captain John Morongo leads and advocates for his community
milestones.context: The Serrano leader served his community, pressed for schooling, and became the figure most closely associated with the reservation’s enduring name.

sources.label: Morongo Band of Mission Indians — About Us
Calisphere — Captain John Morongo

milestones.headline: Hotel Beaumont opens as the boom town’s showpiece
milestones.context: The Queen Anne resort embodied the Southern California Investment Company’s campaign to attract land buyers and visitors to its newly renamed town.

sources.label: Calisphere — Hotel Beaumont
City of Beaumont General Plan — historic setting

milestones.headline: The Woman’s Club organizes—and starts a public library movement
milestones.context: The club assembled a subscription collection in 1909 and then led the campaign for a tax-supported library district before women could vote statewide.

sources.label: Beaumont Library District — About the Library
Calisphere — Beaumont Woman’s Club

milestones.headline: Voters establish the Beaumont Library District
milestones.context: Created by public vote in August, the district opened that October in two rented ground-floor rooms of the Beaumont Bank building.

sources.label: Beaumont Library District — 2024 financial statements, Note 1
Calisphere — Beaumont Bank building

milestones.headline: Beaumont incorporates as a city
milestones.context: On November 18, 1912, the railroad-and-orchard town became an incorporated California city with its own municipal government.

sources.label: City of Beaumont — Your Government

milestones.headline: Beaumont’s Carnegie library opens
milestones.context: The $10,000 Carnegie-funded building opened in June as the library district’s first permanent home and remains in library use.

sources.label: Beaumont Library District — About the Library
Calisphere — Beaumont Carnegie Library image

milestones.headline: Irrigation spreads fruit orchards across Beaumont
milestones.context: New water infrastructure helped replace dry grain land with fruit trees, doubled the population by 1910, and reshaped Beaumont’s economy and identity.

sources.label: City of Beaumont, Existing Conditions Report
Calisphere — H. L. Priest and fruit tree

milestones.headline: Beaumont is promoted as an orchard paradise
milestones.context: The Beaumont Land and Water Company used flowering ranch views like Mellen’s to market irrigated land and make orchards central to the town’s public image.

sources.label: Calisphere — Mellen Ranch orchard
City of Beaumont, Existing Conditions Report

milestones.headline: The Carnegie library expands with its growing district
milestones.context: A rear addition more than doubled the building in 1965, a mansard unified the old and new sections in 1977–78, and a community room followed in 1981.

sources.label: Beaumont Library District — About the Library
Carnegie Libraries of California — Beaumont

milestones.headline: Beaumont remains a compact freeway-era town
milestones.context: Twenty years after the Interstate 10 bypass redirected through traffic, the city still held 6,818 residents within a small grid surrounded by open fields and foothills.

sources.label: City of Beaumont — Housing Element population trends
California Highways — Route 10 history

milestones.headline: Beaumont more than triples in population
milestones.context: Master-planned neighborhoods and freeway-oriented development accompanied growth from 11,384 residents in 2000 to 36,877 in 2010—a 223.9 percent increase.

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau — Population Distribution and Change, 2000 to 2010
U.S. Census Bureau — Beaumont QuickFacts

milestones.headline: The Beaumont Library District marks a century of service
milestones.context: The district celebrated its centennial on August 12, 2011; the restored Carnegie building remained the visible center of a library founded before the city itself.

sources.label: Beaumont Library District — About the Library
Beaumont Library District historical marker chronology
